name: Galilean space-time structure
type_signature: AffineSpace4D with time projection and Euclidean fibers
description: A four-dimensional affine space equipped with a surjective time map to ℝ and a Euclidean metric on each simultaneity fiber, providing the kinematic arena of classical mechanics.

name: Galilean group
type_signature: Group of affine automorphisms preserving Galilean structure
description: The group of all affine transformations of Galilean space-time preserving the time intervals and the spatial Euclidean distance between simultaneous events.

name: Galileo's principle of relativity
description: The laws of mechanics are invariant under the Galilean group, so no inertial frame is physically distinguished from another.

name: Newton's equation of motion
description: The second-order differential equation positing that the acceleration of a point mass is determined by a force function of position, velocity, and time.

name: Newton's principle of determinacy
description: The initial positions and velocities of all points of a mechanical system uniquely determine its entire future and past motion.

name: Galilean invariance constraints on forces
description: Requiring Newton's equations to be Galilean-invariant forces the interaction to depend only on relative positions and relative velocities of the particles and to be invariant under rotations and time translations.

name: Conservative (potential) force field
description: A force field that is the negative gradient of a scalar potential function, so that work done is path-independent.

name: Conservation of momentum
description: For a closed system the total linear momentum is conserved, following from the translational invariance of the Lagrangian.

name: Conservation of angular momentum
description: For a system invariant under rotations the total angular momentum about the center is conserved, following from rotational invariance of the Lagrangian.

name: Period of one-dimensional motion (energy integral)
description: The period of oscillation of a one-degree-of-freedom conservative system expressed as an integral over the classically allowed region between turning points.

name: Reduction of the two-body problem (reduced mass)
description: The two-body problem with central interaction separates into free motion of the center of mass and motion of a single particle of reduced mass μ in a central field.

name: Reduction of central motion via angular momentum
function_signature: (central force motion in ℝ³) → (one-dimensional radial motion)
description: Uses conservation of angular momentum to confine motion to a plane and eliminate the angular variable, reducing a central-field problem to a single radial degree of freedom.

name: Effective potential
description: The sum of the true potential and the centrifugal term M²/(2μr²) governing the equivalent one-dimensional radial motion in a central field.

name: Orbit equation of central motion (quadrature)
description: The closed-form expression of the orbit shape φ(r) for central motion obtained by integrating the radial and angular equations.

name: Kepler's problem
description: The central-field problem with an inverse-square attractive force, whose bounded orbits are conics with the center of force at a focus.

name: Laplace–Runge–Lenz vector
description: A conserved vector specific to the inverse-square central field, pointing along the major axis and encoding the orientation and eccentricity of the orbit.

name: Analysis of fall to the center
function_signature: (central potential, energy, angular momentum) → (collision vs. bounded vs. escape verdict)
description: Determines whether a particle in a central field spirals into the center in finite time by comparing the potential's singularity with the centrifugal barrier.

name: Generalized (canonical) momentum
description: The momentum conjugate to a generalized coordinate, defined as the partial derivative of the Lagrangian with respect to the corresponding velocity.

name: Cyclic coordinates and Routh reduction
description: When a coordinate is cyclic (absent from the Lagrangian) its conjugate momentum is conserved, and Routh's procedure eliminates it to obtain a reduced Lagrangian system in the remaining coordinates.

name: Holonomic constraint
description: A constraint expressible as equations relating only the coordinates (and possibly time), confining motion to a submanifold of configuration space.

name: D'Alembert–Lagrange principle
description: The principle that the total virtual work of the constraint forces vanishes for all virtual displacements compatible with the constraints, yielding the equations of constrained motion.

name: Lagrangian mechanics on a manifold
description: The formulation of Lagrangian dynamics for a system whose configuration space is a smooth manifold, with the Lagrangian a function on the tangent bundle and motions the critical curves of the action.

name: Legendre transformation (Lagrangian to Hamiltonian)
description: Passes from the Lagrangian on the tangent bundle to the Hamiltonian on the cotangent bundle by replacing velocities with conjugate momenta via fiberwise convex duality.

name: Small oscillations / linearization about equilibrium
function_signature: (Lagrangian, stable equilibrium) → (linear system of coupled oscillators)
description: Approximates motion near a stable equilibrium by expanding the kinetic and potential energies to quadratic order, yielding a linear system of coupled harmonic oscillators.

name: Normal modes and characteristic frequencies
description: Small oscillations of a system about stable equilibrium decompose into independent harmonic normal modes whose characteristic frequencies are the roots of the generalized eigenvalue equation det(K - ω²M)=0.

name: Simultaneous diagonalization of two quadratic forms
function_signature: (positive-definite form T, symmetric form U) → (basis diagonalizing both)
description: Finds a single linear change of coordinates that simultaneously diagonalizes a positive-definite quadratic form and another symmetric form, used to decouple the kinetic and potential energies.

name: Parametric resonance
description: A system whose parameters vary periodically in time can be destabilized, with the trivial equilibrium becoming unstable when the driving frequency is near twice a natural frequency divided by an integer.

name: Rigid-body configuration space SO(3)
description: The configuration space of a rigid body fixed at a point is the rotation group SO(3), and of a free rigid body the group of orientation-preserving Euclidean motions.

name: Inertia tensor
type_signature: I : ℝ³ → ℝ³ symmetric positive operator
description: The symmetric positive operator on the body frame relating angular velocity to angular momentum, encoding the mass distribution of a rigid body.

name: Principal axes of inertia
description: The orthogonal eigenframe of the inertia tensor, in which the inertia operator is diagonal with the principal moments of inertia as eigenvalues.

name: Angular velocity in body and space frames
description: The angular velocity vector of a rotating rigid body expressed in the rotating body frame and in the fixed space frame, related by the body's current rotation.

name: Euler's equations for a rigid body
description: The equations of motion of a rigid body in the body frame, equating the rate of change of angular momentum plus its gyroscopic term to the applied torque.

name: Euler angles
description: A triple of angles parametrizing the orientation of a rigid body as a composition of three successive rotations, giving local coordinates on SO(3).

name: Poinsot's construction (inertia ellipsoid)
description: The free rotation of a rigid body is described geometrically as the inertia ellipsoid rolling without slipping on a fixed plane perpendicular to the conserved angular momentum.

name: Lagrange top (heavy symmetric top)
description: A heavy symmetric rigid body fixed at a point on its symmetry axis, an integrable case whose motion combines precession, nutation, and spin.

name: Stability of rotation about principal axes
description: Steady rotation of a free rigid body about the axes of largest and smallest moment of inertia is stable, while rotation about the intermediate axis is unstable.

name: Poincaré–Cartan integral invariant
description: The 1-form p dq - H dt whose integral around any closed curve in extended phase space is preserved by the Hamiltonian flow, characterizing the canonical structure.

name: Relative and absolute integral invariants
description: An integral over a cycle is an absolute integral invariant of a flow if preserved over arbitrary cycles and relative if preserved only over boundaries, with the canonical 1-form and symplectic form furnishing the basic Hamiltonian examples.

name: Separation of variables in the Hamilton–Jacobi equation
function_signature: (separable Hamiltonian, coordinate choice) → (complete integral as sum of single-variable terms)
description: Seeks a complete integral of the Hamilton–Jacobi equation as a sum of functions each depending on one coordinate, reducing the PDE to decoupled quadratures and exhibiting the system as integrable.

name: Euler equations on a Lie algebra
description: The generalization of the rigid-body and ideal-fluid equations as the flow on the dual of a Lie algebra generated by a left-invariant quadratic energy via the coadjoint action.

name: Geodesics on Lie groups (hydrodynamics analogy)
description: Geodesics of a one-sided invariant Riemannian metric on a Lie group satisfy the Euler equations on its Lie algebra, unifying rigid-body rotation with ideal fluid motion on the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group.

name: Lie–Poisson structure on the dual of a Lie algebra
description: The natural Poisson bracket on the dual of a Lie algebra induced by the Lie bracket, whose symplectic leaves are the coadjoint orbits.

name: Small denominators problem
description: The obstruction in perturbation theory of quasi-periodic motion arising from near-resonant frequency combinations k·ω that can make formal series diverge unless the frequencies satisfy Diophantine conditions.

name: Adiabatic invariant
description: Identifies the action variable of a one-degree-of-freedom oscillator as approximately conserved under slow variation of the system's parameters.

name: Canonical perturbation theory
function_signature: (near-integrable Hamiltonian) → (canonical transformation simplifying it order by order)
description: Constructs canonical transformations by generating functions to remove the perturbation order by order in action-angle variables for a nearly integrable Hamiltonian system.

name: Caustic (Lagrangian singularity)
description: The singular set of the projection of a Lagrangian submanifold to configuration space, where infinitely many rays or trajectories focus and short-wave amplitudes blow up.

name: Short-wave (WKB) asymptotics with Maslov index
description: Constructs short-wavelength asymptotic solutions of wave equations from a Lagrangian submanifold, with phase shifts at caustics fixed by the Maslov index to make the global expansion well defined.

name: Extended phase space
description: The phase space enlarged by the time variable and its conjugate momentum -H, on which a time-dependent Hamiltonian system becomes autonomous and the Poincaré–Cartan form is the canonical 1-form.
